main_text.l: tuta municipalia. Iacobi 6. Paral.6. statuto 92a &
parlam. 11. statut. 47. Præsertim vero stat. 106. parl.
7. Iacobi 6, anno 1581. quibus expresse mandatur,
supremarum curiarum judicibus, ut in omnibus
causis quæ ad illa fora pertinent dijudicandis, intre-
pide procedant; easdemque sublata omni cuncta-
tione definiant, latamque sententiam executioni
mandent, non obstante quolibet Regis mandato
aut rescripto in contrarium: nihilque quotidiana
hujus praxi in curiis illis usitatius: nam nisi singula
causarum genera ad proprium forum referantur,
mera obtinebit ἀτελία, ac nisi curiis illis supremis
libertas hæc illibata constet, sub umbra promoven-
di jus regale, regnaret injustitia: Quæ eum locum
habeant in sæcularibus curiis; potiori jure synodo
nationali legitime convocatæ & formatæ compe-
tunt; utpote cui, supremam potestatem controver-
sias omnes ecclesiasticas determinandi afferant vel
ipsi Hierarchici, Theologi videl. Magnæ Britan-
niæ ad Synodum Dordracenam deputati, in judicio
suo de Remonstrantium protestatione: qua senten-
tia non putabant se juri regio detrahere, aut Papatu-
i in Synodi persona renovare, quæ opinionem hanc
nunc modeste tuentibus atrociter objiciuntur, ab
iis qui struunt de proprio calumnias innocentiæ; &
quod nondum auf sunt Antiqui Papatus monstrum
aperta facie omnibus adorandum reponere, sub
velo supremorum Magistratuum obtrudunt, eorum-
que spiritu beftiam illam extrema spirantem, re-
focillare, ejusque vulnera mortalia obligare, nequi-
cquam fatagunt. Denique ad illud quo omnibus
mandatur subscriptio fœderis & confessionis juxta
sensum & Declarationem à Marchione Regis no-
mine publicatam, Respondent; Senfum illum non
esse genuinum, sed confessioni affixum, contrarium
publicæ professioni & praxi majorum Confessioni

page.notes: Transcription is from a 16th–17th century Latin text with some Greek (ἀτελία is rendered from the scan's Greek word, which the scan shows as a short Greek form; treat as uncertain). Several words are blurred or partly obscured at the line ends and in the lower part of the page; "primi-" is a line-end hyphenated word continuing onto the next page. Letters with long s have been normalised to plain s per the rules. Some words may be misread; where I was not sure I should have marked them [?], and the lower lines near the bottom are particularly faint and should be checked against the scan.
